title: Oxygenation on Escalating Support
scenario: A 64-year-old client with pneumonia is monitored over six hours. Despite increasing oxygen support, the nurse tracks the client's oxygenation and respiratory status on the flowsheet.

questions.subject: Medical-Surgical
questions.stem: Interpreting the respiratory flowsheet, which statement best describes the trend?

options.text: Oxygen saturation continues to fall and work of breathing worsens despite escalating oxygen support, indicating refractory hypoxemia
The client is improving because oxygen support is being provided
The stable respiratory rate shows the client is compensating well
The findings reflect anxiety rather than a physiologic problem

questions.rationale: Even as support increases from 2 L to a non-rebreather, the SpO2 keeps dropping while respiratory rate and work of breathing climb, which signals worsening, treatment-refractory hypoxemia and impending respiratory failure.

questions.subject: Medical-Surgical
questions.stem: Based on the deteriorating trend at 16:00, which nursing actions are appropriate? Select all that apply.

options.text: Notify the provider and rapid response team urgently
Position the client upright to maximize lung expansion
Prepare for possible escalation to non-invasive ventilation or intubation
Obtain an arterial blood gas as ordered
Remove all supplemental oxygen to assess room-air tolerance
Reassure the client and recheck oxygenation in two hours

questions.rationale: Refractory hypoxemia on maximal mask oxygen requires urgent escalation, upright positioning, preparation for advanced airway support, and an ABG. Removing oxygen or delaying reassessment would be dangerous.
